title: Install two RAM sticks (Franka, operational-space control)
text:
A gaming-PC case lying on its side on a sturdy table, opening up, its motherboard facing the ceiling. All four memory slots are empty. Beside the case two loose RAM sticks stand upright in foam holders, already in their installation orientation.
Goal: grip each stick by its top edge, lift it straight out of its holder, carry it over the case wall, line its gold edge connector up with its slot — the outermost and the second-from-socket, the alternating pair a dual-channel kit fills (the notch only fits one way — heat-spreader faces along the slot) — and press it straight down until it clicks fully home. A seated stick stays put on its own. The task is complete once both sticks are fully seated. A stick holds in a firm pinch: close the fingers flat across its faces near the top edge and the grip locks; open wide to release.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run, each RAM stick is pressed into its own DIMM slot: the stick starting in the holder farther from the robot base goes in the outermost slot (farthest from the CPU socket), the other in the second-from-socket slot. For each, in the fixed case's frame (board face horizontal, facing up), the bottom-centre of the stick's gold edge connector is at most 0.9456 mm above the board face, i.e. at least 3.7 mm below the slot's wall top 4.6456 mm above the face (it bottoms out at 0.2058 mm), and within 3 mm horizontally of its seated point; its up axis is within 6° of the board normal and its length axis within 3° of the slot heading it already has standing in its holder (not reversed). Not true at the start. [success() = seated().all(); stick k must seat in slot k; seated points world (0.40731, -0.06789, 0.02911), (0.42627, -0.06789, 0.02911)]
